assumptions: The selected rice, pasta, chickpea or lentil preparation can be completed within ninety active minutes.
Thursday and Friday portions are frozen promptly and safely reheated.
Different combinations of the same protein, energy and fresh component provide acceptable variety.
proposals.proposal: Thermally transform an energy base such as rice or pasta during the batch cook, distribute a chickpea or lentil protein base across five portions, and reuse a quick fresh vegetable component with different combinations. Eat refrigerated portions Monday through Wednesday and freeze the remaining portions for Thursday and Friday.
proposals.reason: This ordered proposal directly supports a practical five-evening plan: batch cooking supplies the energy and protein, while the reused fresh component creates weekday variation. The refrigeration and freezing schedule satisfies the three-day storage limit, and the plan is clear enough to execute within the stated preparation ceiling if the batch quantities remain modest.

assumptions: Protein and energy bases can be batch-cooked within ninety active minutes.
Chickpeas or lentils provide the planned protein base.

proposals.proposal: Distribute the protein base across five portions, allocate the preparation capacity between batch cooking and one quick fresh component, distribute energy bases such as rice and pasta across the weekdays, and combine them with tomatoes and seasonal vegetables. Refrigerate Monday through Wednesday meals and freeze Thursday and Friday meals, using different combinations to create variety.
proposals.reason: The ordered sequence gives the strongest complete structure: protein coverage, bounded preparation, varied energy bases, and final meal assembly. It can satisfy coverage, time and storage constraints, though distributing both protein and energy bases may require more cooking and portion management than the ninety-minute limit allows unless the bases are batch-cooked efficiently.

assumptions: The batch can be portioned into five complete evening meals.

proposals.reason: The ordered sequence directly manages preparation capacity and delayed use, yielding a practical five-evening schedule with storage compliance and moderate variety. It is less explicit about the actual weekday order and relies on proposed portioning and accompaniments to make the meals complete.
